title: Childhood Confessions
blurb: Playground deals, sibling blame and the things you got away with as a kid.

prompts: cut my own hair as a kid and tried to hide it
blamed a sibling for something I definitely did
pretended to be sick to stay home from school
eaten glue, crayon or play dough
had an imaginary friend
snuck a peek at my presents before Christmas or my birthday
hidden vegetables under my plate or fed them to the dog
written my name somewhere I definitely should not have
been sent to the principal's office
run away from home, even if it was only to the end of the street
forged a parent's signature on a school note
gotten my head or arm stuck somewhere it did not belong
had a sleepover where nobody actually slept
thrown a tantrum in the middle of a supermarket
traded something valuable in the playground for something worthless
read under the covers with a torch way past bedtime
broken something at home and hidden the pieces
made a secret pact with a best friend that I have since broken
been terrified of a monster in my room that turned out to be a pile of clothes
gotten lost in a shopping centre and been called out over the speakers
cried at the end of a kids' movie
eaten a whole bag of lollies and then felt very sick
pretended to be asleep in the car so I would be carried inside
turned up to school in costume on the wrong day
tried to dig a hole to the other side of the world
gone through a phase I would hate to see on video now
begged for a toy for months and then played with it once
gotten my tongue stuck to something frozen
believed that adults knew absolutely everything
had a pet that "went to live on a farm"
copied an older sibling or cousin's style head to toe
put on a concert or play in the lounge room and made the whole family watch
lost a tooth in my dinner and nearly swallowed it
believed swallowing a seed would grow a tree in my stomach
pretended to read a book for school by only looking at the pictures
used a chore chart for exactly one week
been scared of the plughole when the bath emptied
played "the floor is lava" and treated it as a matter of life and death
swapped stickers or cards at school and felt ripped off afterwards
built a fort out of couch cushions and refused to come out for dinner
kept a rock collection or a jar of bugs like it was treasure
cried because my ice cream fell off the cone
had a haircut from a parent armed with the kitchen scissors
asked a very loud, very embarrassing question in front of a stranger
held my breath through a tunnel or past a cemetery
mixed every flavour at the soft drink machine into one cup
written a letter to Santa, the tooth fairy or a pop star and waited for a reply
pretended I couldn't hear my parents calling me in for dinner
